newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: No repairs yet on crippled Colombian pipeline.
newsitem.headline: No repairs yet on crippled Colombian pipeline.

text.p: Repair work has yet to begin on Colombia's dynamite-damaged Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline but it may get underway Thursday afternoon, the state oil company Ecopetrol said.

A company spokesman said the army had secured the region where rebel dynamite charges damaged at least two segments of the pipeline and Ecopetrol work crews were preparing to enter the area later Thursday.
Before any repairs are actually carried out, he said a team of specialists would have to assess damage to the structure, however.
"We have to await results of the on-site inspection," he said of the upcoming repair work and when it might be completed.
Crude production from the 180,000 barrel per day Cao Limn field, operated by Occidental Petroleum Corp, has been shut-in for the last 11 days because of repeated bombings by leftist guerrillas.

On Tuesday Occidental was forced to declare force majeure on the Cao Limn field. Ecopetrol, Occidental partner in the field, has also been forced to declare force majeure on the delivery of at least two crude shipments that were due to be dispatched from the Caribbean port of Coveas.
